description: Nous avons nommé notre projet IRCO, pour Intelligent Remote Care Operations. Parce que dans l'espace, les astronautes ne peuvent pas se permettre d'attendre les ordres de la Terre. IRCO, c'est l'alliance d'une Intelligence artificielle autonome, d'une surveillance à distance sans faille, pour garantir la prise en charge médicale de l'équipage, le tout intégré dans les opérations critiques de la mission.
summary: IRCO is a health-monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions, where Earth communication delays (up to ~20 min one way on Mars) force crews to interpret their own health data. A deterministic rules engine, written in Rust, ingests indicators (heart rate, sleep, fatigue, cabin CO2, radiation), compares each value with the astronaut's personal baseline and trends, and produces a traceable green/amber/red vigilance level with the exact rules that triggered it. An explanatory layer (search over NASA HRP and CSA sources with citations, plus an optional multimodal AI engine running on a GPU notebook) explains why an indicator matters and when to contact the flight surgeon. The AI never sets or changes the vigilance level, and the system keeps working without it. Every value carries a data class (measured_real, analog, synthetic) and every threshold a status (provisional); missing data is shown as "no data", never as normal. The demo uses a synthetic astronaut (A-01, mission day 124) clearly labelled as simulated. IRCO is decision support, not a diagnosis.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

IRCO helps an astronaut observe, compare, detect and understand health changes during a long mission. It ingests indicators, stores them with provenance, evaluates deterministic rules (absolute thresholds, deviation from the personal baseline, trend slope, persistence, missing-data and composite rules) and returns a vigilance level (green, amber, red, no data) with the triggered rules, the data quality and the recommended action, including when to contact the flight surgeon.

HOW IT WORKS

- Backend: Rust (axum, SQLite), versioned REST API with OpenAPI, rules in a JSON file reloadable without recompiling.

- Frontend: web dashboard that only displays what the API returns; it never computes a status.

- Knowledge: offline BM25 search over summaries of NASA HRP and Canadian Space Agency pages, each answer cited or marked "source not found".

- AI engine (optional): multimodal GPU notebook (chat Qwen3-4B, speech-to-text Whisper, text-to-speech MMS-TTS, vision-language SmolVLM). It explains and transcribes only; it has no route to the vigilance engine. If it is offline, the assistant falls back to cited extracts and the monitoring continues.

- Demo: replayable synthetic scenario A-01 (days 1 to 124): green at day 1, amber at day 97, red at day 117.

TRUTHFULNESS BY DESIGN

Each observation is labelled measured_real, analog or synthetic. Thresholds are illustrative and marked provisional. Missing or suspect data never counts as normal. Real cabin telemetry (ISS, NASA OSDR RR-1) and space weather (NOAA SWPC) are displayed as environment context, not as astronaut health.

LIMITS

Thresholds are not clinically validated. Astronaut physiology in the demo is synthetic. The knowledge base is small. Voice and vision run in the notebook and are not yet integrated into the API. IRCO is decision support, not a diagnosis.

INTENDED IMPACT

Greater crew autonomy when ground support is delayed, with explainable, auditable alerts.

CREATIVITY

Strict separation between a deterministic decision engine and an explanatory AI, with data-class labelling shown to the user at every level.
